An emulator for a comptuer from 1973, with 4KB of RAM, running a slimmed down version of BASIC originally made for calculators that can do three monitors: Check

Bonus: Hardware configuration.

  • Slots 1, 4 and 5 are three monitors, latched at addresses 005, 006 and 007 respectively, which is the system's capacity; Three monitors, at 80 by 24 letters each, for a total of 5760 lettes, 1920 letters for each screen.

  • Slot 0 is the keyboard. If you're malicious, set this as someone's console output and watch them get confused.

  • Slot 2 is the disk controller, armed here with two drives, out of four possible. The system can take a total of twelve drives across three controllers.

  • Slot 3 is the printer controller. You could write up a program, and in each line write parts of your school essay, and print it out to a printer via configuring the printing output here, which defaults to the first screen, as with console output.

Bonus historical info:

  • The guy who founded the company was the one who invented a device called a pulse transfer controlling device, which in turn made magnetic core memory possible, which in turn paved the way for modern HDDs as we know them, back in 1948. Wang Laboratories was founded around this patent, which was known for both their word processing machines and their calculators, the 2200 being their first ever full-fledged computer.
